sections.content:
We use **algo** (something, anything) and **nada** (nothing, not anything) for inanimate objects or concepts.

• **Double Negation**: When *nada* is placed after the verb, use *no* before the verb:
  *No quiero nada de comer.*
• When *nada* is the subject or precedes the verb, do not use *no*:
  *Nada es imposible.*
• **Common expressions**: *algo de* (a little bit of), *nada de* (none of / not at all), *de nada* (you're welcome).

items.spanish: ¿Quieres comer algo antes de ir al cine?
items.english: Do you want to eat something before going to the movies?

items.spanish: No encontramos nada interesante en la tienda.
items.english: We didn't find anything interesting in the shop.

items.spanish: Nada me molesta tanto como el ruido.
items.english: Nothing bothers me as much as noise.

sections.content: Use *algo de* before non-count nouns: *algo de agua* (a little water), *algo de tiempo* (some time).
